explain.say: CNC stands for computer numerical control. A CNC mill carves a part out of a solid block of metal or plastic, following instructions instead of a person's hands.

faq.q: What are the axes on a CNC machine?
faq.a: A basic mill has three axes: X for left and right, Y for forward and back, and Z for up and down. Five-axis machines also tilt and rotate, so the cutter can reach complex shapes from many angles.
asks: What is a five-axis CNC machine?

faq.a: Computer-aided manufacturing software takes a 3D design and works out the cutting tool's paths, depths and speeds, then writes them out as G-code for the machine.
asks: How does a CNC machine know what to cut?

faq.q: How accurate is a CNC machine?
faq.a: Typical CNC machines cut to within about a hundredth of a millimetre, and precision machines do even better. They can repeat the same part thousands of times.

faq.q: What is the difference between CNC and 3D printing?
faq.a: CNC machining is subtractive: it cuts material away from a solid block. 3D printing is additive: it builds the object up layer by layer. Both follow G-code.
asks: Is CNC the same as 3D printing?

faq.q: Why does a CNC machine spray liquid?
faq.a: Cutting metal makes heat. Coolant sprayed at the cutter keeps the tool and the part cool, washes away chips and helps give a smooth finish.

facts: Numerical control of machine tools was developed at MIT in the early 1950s with US Air Force funding.
Five-axis CNC machines can tilt and rotate the tool or the part as well as moving along X, Y and Z.

quiz.say: What does CAM software do in CNC machining?
quiz.why: CAM turns a 3D design into toolpaths and G-code that the machine follows.
